To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a deep network can be trained to directly produce time-domain clean speech and this approach significantly outperforms previous methods.

the proposed deep neural network (1) directly reconstructs the clean speech from time-frequency masked spectrograms, (2) outperforms a state-of-the-art non-negative matrix factorisation based speech separation system in objective intelligibility and quality, and (3) is trained jointly with speech resynthesis and ideal mask estimation.

a deep neural network for signal reconstruction outperforms a non-negative matrix factoration based system in terms of objective intelligibility and quality, and the proposed system achieves a 1.2% absolute word error rate improvement on the CHiME-4 dataset over the state of the art.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of separating the target speech from the mixture of target speech and noise.
a new deep network structure and training method for speech enhancement and separation.
the development of a deep neural network for speech enhancement, which is a key component in speech separation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system achieves a new state-of-the-art performance on the CHiME3 dataset.
the proposed system achieves the highest speech intelligibility and the highest quality in the state-of-the-art.
our proposed time domain network achieves better objective quality while maintaining similar objective intelligibility performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed system can achieve better objective intelligibility performance than the non-negative matrix factoration system, while maintaining the objective quality performance.

the proposed method is a simple yet effective way to improve the objective speech quality without compromising speech intelligibility, which is an important step towards a more practical and robust separation system.
we have developed an end-to-end deep network for speech separation, and it achieves the state-of-the-art performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a DNN based separation system, it may be more effective to directly estimate the time-domain speech than to first estimate a time-frequency mask.
, with a proper network structure, a DNN can be trained to perform time-domain signal reconstruction, which is a promising direction for future research.
the DNN-based separation can be extended to the time domain, which is more convenient for practical implementation.
